title: MSI health
description: Host health of the MSI home server: power and GPU, temperatures, battery, disk, network, CPU and memory, server hygiene, backups and app health. Provisioned from git; edit the JSON file.

list.name: other_w
list.label: Rest of laptop (W, model)
list.description: Power of everything except the CPU package, used by the estimated total. 4.6 W measured idle on battery on 2026-11-05. Change it after a new measurement.

list.name: ab_window
list.label: A/B window
list.description: Length of the two windows compared in the A/B panel.

list.name: ab_offset
list.label: A/B offset
list.description: How far before now window B is.

panels.title: CPU package
panels.description: Hottest point of the CPU. Yellow from 85 °C, red from 95 °C (the CPU throttles itself at 100 °C).

panels.title: NVMe SSD
panels.description: SSD 'Composite' temperature. Yellow from 82.8 °C (the drive's own warning limit), red from 84.85 °C (its critical limit).

panels.title: Battery
panels.description: Battery charge level.

panels.title: Power source
panels.description: Is the mains adapter (ADP1) connected? 'On battery' means the laptop is running from its battery: a power cut or an unplugged charger.

panels.title: Root disk free
panels.description: Free space on / for normal users. Yellow under ~140 GB (about 70 % used), red under ~93 GB (about 80 % used).

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since the MSI last booted.

panels.title: Wall (plug meter)
panels.description: Real consumption at the socket, charger losses included. Needs a plug-in power meter with a local exporter (metric msi_wall_power_watts). None is installed: see docs/GPU_AND_POWER.md.

panels.title: Est. total (model)
panels.description: Model, not a measurement: CPU package power (RAPL) + $other_w W for everything else. $other_w = battery discharge (7.9 W) minus CPU package (3.3 W), measured idle, on battery, 2026-11-05 09:31-09:44 UTC. Valid only near idle; excludes charger losses. A plug meter is the only real total. This is the best available guess of what the charger delivers.

panels.title: CPU package (RAPL)
panels.description: Measured: power of the CPU package (cores, integrated GPU, memory controller) from the CPU's RAPL energy counter. Does NOT include the NVIDIA GPU, screen, SSD, Wi-Fi, fans or the charger.

panels.title: Battery discharging
panels.description: Measured: current x voltage of the battery, shown ONLY when the charger is unplugged; then it is the whole laptop's consumption. On mains the battery supplies nothing, so there is nothing to show.

panels.title: GPU state
panels.description: Runtime power state of the RTX 3060 (0000:01:00.0), read from sysfs without waking it. Off (D3cold) = power removed by the platform: the normal state on this server.

panels.title: GPU time off (range)
panels.description: Share of the selected time range the NVIDIA GPU spent suspended (powered off). 99.97 % on 2026-11-05.

panels.title: Price now (PVPC)
panels.description: Spanish regulated consumer price (PVPC) for the current hour, energy term only, without taxes or the fixed power term. From Red Eléctrica's public API (apidatos.ree.es), refreshed every 15 min by price-fetch. It is NOT necessarily your own tariff. Optional: needs the pvpc profile.

panels.title: PVPC today
panels.description: Cheapest, average and most expensive hour of today (Spain).

panels.title: Energy in range (est.)
panels.description: Estimated total energy over the selected time range: CPU package energy (measured, RAPL) + $other_w W x duration (model). In kWh.

panels.title: Cost in range (est.)
panels.description: Estimated total power x the PVPC price of each moment, added up over the selected range (5-minute steps). Estimate: the power is a model and the price may not be your tariff. Taxes and fixed terms not included.

panels.title: Cost per month (est.)
panels.description: Estimated total power averaged over the last hour, x 24 h x 30 days, x today's mean PVPC. A projection, not a bill.

panels.title: Price data age
panels.description: Minutes since Red Eléctrica's API last answered. Turns yellow after 30 min, red after 2 h (the price shown may be stale or missing).

panels.title: Power
panels.description: Measured: CPU package and cores (RAPL); battery W only while unplugged. Model: estimated total. psys is shown for reference only: on this laptop it reads far BELOW the real total (0.2 W on battery while the battery gave 7.9 W), so it is not the platform total. Orange marks = experiments.

panels.title: Electricity price
panels.description: PVPC (regulated consumer price, hourly) and the wholesale spot price (15 min), EUR/kWh, from Red Eléctrica. Energy term only, no taxes.

panels.title: NVIDIA GPU power state
panels.description: Green = powered off (D3cold), red = awake. gpu = the graphics chip, gpu_audio = its HDMI audio, gpu_bridge = the CPU's PCIe port it hangs from. lspci, ubuntu-drivers or reading the PCIe link speed wake it for a few seconds.

panels.title: NVIDIA GPU: seconds awake per hour
panels.description: How long the GPU was awake in each hour. Near 0 = it sleeps; a step up shows when something woke it.

panels.title: A/B: average power, A = last $ab_window, B = $ab_offset earlier
panels.description: Compare two windows of the same length to see the effect of a change. A ends now; B is the same length, $ab_offset earlier. Choose both at the top (A/B window, A/B offset). Battery shows 0 while on mains. Discard the first minutes after a change.

defaults.noValue: No data in one of the windows

panels.title: CPU temperature
panels.description: Package = whole chip (the number that matters). Thin lines = individual cores. Dashed lines: 85 °C warning, 95 °C critical.

panels.title: NVMe SSD temperature
panels.description: Composite = the drive's overall temperature (use this one). Sensor 1 = an internal sensor. Dashed lines: 82.8 °C warning, 84.85 °C critical (limits reported by the drive itself).

panels.title: Wi-Fi and board sensors
panels.description: Wi-Fi card (iwlwifi) and ACPI thermal zones from the laptop firmware. x86_pkg_temp repeats the CPU package; TCPU/TCPU_PCI are CPU-area sensors; SEN2/SEN3 are board sensors whose exact location MSI does not document. No thresholds: the hardware publishes no limits for these.

panels.title: Min > 85 °C (24 h)
panels.description: Minutes in the last 24 h with the CPU package above 85 °C (warning level).

panels.title: Min > 90 °C (24 h)
panels.description: Minutes in the last 24 h with the CPU package above 90 °C.

panels.title: Throttling (range)
panels.description: Times the CPU slowed itself down for heat during the selected range (kernel thermal_throttle counter). A few during heavy builds are normal; many while idle mean poor cooling.

panels.title: EC mode
panels.description: Embedded controller performance mode (msi-ec shift_mode): eco, comfort or turbo.

panels.title: GPU fan / EC GPU temp
panels.description: The embedded controller's view of the NVIDIA GPU. 0 % and 0 °C = GPU powered off.

panels.title: Cooler boost
panels.description: EC 'cooler boost' (fans at full speed). Normally off.

panels.title: Fans (embedded controller)
panels.description: Fan speed reported by the EC through msi-ec, percent.

panels.title: Thermal throttling events per hour
panels.description: CPU package slow-downs for heat, counted per hour.

panels.title: Charging state
panels.description: What the battery reports: Charging, Discharging, Full or 'Not charging' (plugged in but held below the charge limit set in firmware).

panels.title: Battery health
panels.description: Capacity when full today divided by capacity when new (charge_full / charge_full_design). Yellow under 70 %, red under 50 %.

panels.title: Full charge capacity
panels.description: Charge the battery holds when full now, and when it was new.

panels.title: Cycle count
panels.description: Charge cycles reported by the battery. This MSI firmware reports 0, which means 'not available', not 'new battery'.

panels.title: Battery level
panels.description: Charge level over time. With the firmware charge limit it should sit around the limit while plugged in; a falling line means it is running on battery.

panels.title: Battery current × voltage (0 W on mains)
panels.description: Current x voltage of the battery. On mains this is 0 W: the battery is idle, NOT the laptop's consumption (see the Power and GPU row). It shows the real consumption only while the charger is unplugged.

panels.title: Power source history
panels.description: Green = on mains, red = on battery. A red stripe is a power cut or an unplugged charger.

panels.title: Root filesystem used
panels.description: Used space on / (same number as 'df -h /'). Yellow from 70 %, red from 80 %.

panels.title: Free space
panels.description: Space available to normal users on each real filesystem.

panels.title: Disk throughput
panels.description: Bytes per second read from (up) and written to (down) the SSD.

panels.title: Disk I/O time
panels.description: Fraction of time the SSD had work in progress. Short peaks are normal; staying near 100 % for minutes means the disk is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Root filesystem used over time
panels.description: Watch the trend: a steady climb tells you when the disk will be full. Dashed lines at 70 % and 80 %.

panels.title: Days until / is full
panels.description: Linear forecast from the last 3 days of free space. 'Not filling up' when free space is not shrinking. Noisy with little history or after a big one-off download.

panels.title: Free space in 30 days (forecast)
panels.description: predict_linear over the last 3 days: free space on / expected in 30 days if the trend continues.

panels.title: Prometheus storage
panels.description: Metric history on disk (blocks + write-ahead log). Hard cap 10 GB: above it the oldest data is deleted.

panels.title: CPU frequency (avg / max)
panels.description: Current clock of the 20 threads: average and highest. Helps read the CPU power.

panels.title: Link state
panels.description: UP = the interface is connected (cable plugged in / Wi-Fi associated).

panels.title: Link state history
panels.description: Green = up, red = down. Shows when the cable or Wi-Fi dropped.

panels.title: Traffic
panels.description: Bits per second received (up) and transmitted (down) on each interface.

panels.title: Errors and drops
panels.description: Packets per second that failed (errors) or were discarded (drops). Should be 0 almost always. Errors on enp4s0 often mean a bad cable or port; a small steady rate of receive drops (well under 1/s) is normal: the kernel discards frames for protocols this machine does not use.

panels.title: Active uplink
panels.description: The interface that carries the default route (how the MSI reaches the internet).

panels.title: Cable link changes (range)
panels.description: Times the cable (enp4s0) link went up or down in the selected range (each unplug counts twice).

panels.title: Tailscale link
panels.description: Carrier of the tailscale0 interface (node_network_up reads 0 for it because its operstate is 'unknown').

panels.title: Wi-Fi link changes (range)
panels.description: Times the Wi-Fi (wlo1) link went up or down in the selected range.

panels.title: CPU busy
panels.description: Average use of all 20 CPU threads. Yellow from 70 %, red from 90 %.

panels.title: Memory used
panels.description: RAM in use that cannot be freed instantly (total minus 'available'). Yellow from 80 %, red from 90 %.

panels.title: Swap used
panels.description: Swap (disk used as overflow RAM). A little is fine; yellow from 1 GiB, red from 3 GiB of the 4 GiB.

panels.title: Load (1 min)
panels.description: Processes running or waiting for CPU/disk. With 20 threads, under ~14 is relaxed; yellow from 14, red from 20 (more work than threads).

panels.title: CPU usage by type
panels.description: Average over all threads, stacked. user = programs, system = kernel, iowait = waiting for the disk.

panels.title: Load average
panels.description: 1, 5 and 15 minute load. The dashed line is the number of CPU threads (20).

panels.title: Memory and swap
panels.description: used = RAM in use; available = RAM that can still be given to programs (includes cache that Linux frees on demand); swap used should stay near 0.

panels.title: Last backup age
panels.description: Hours since the last SUCCESSFUL backup (a status file written by the backup job into the textfile folder, TEXTFILE_HOST_DIR). Red above 26 h.

panels.title: Last backup result
panels.description: Result of the last backup run.

panels.title: Last restore test age
panels.description: Days since a restore test last succeeded. Needs the restore test to write homelab_restore_test_last_success_timestamp_seconds into the textfile folder.

panels.title: Battery charge limits
panels.description: Firmware charge thresholds: expected start 50 % / end 60 %. 'CHANGED' means the limit was lost (e.g. after a firmware reset).

panels.title: Updates pending
panels.description: Package updates available (update-notifier, refreshed about daily).

panels.title: Security updates
panels.description: Security updates available.

panels.title: Reboot required
panels.description: A package update asked for a reboot (/run/reboot-required).

panels.title: msi-ec module
panels.description: The msi-ec driver (charge limits, fans) is loaded.

panels.title: NVIDIA driver
panels.description: Kernel driver of the NVIDIA GPU (nouveau = open driver; the proprietary one is not installed by decision).

panels.title: Collector age
panels.description: Seconds since textfile-gen last wrote its file. Above 60 s the GPU, fan and hygiene panels are stale.

panels.title: App health
panels.description: GET of the URLs in prometheus/targets/apphealth.yml every 30 s (blackbox_exporter, profile apphealth). Up = HTTP 2xx.

panels.title: App response time
panels.description: Time to answer each health check, including the database check.

panels.title: HTTP status
panels.description: Last HTTP status code of each check (200 = OK).
